question: While it is now recognised that third countries use migrants to threaten EU Member States, NGOs are often spared any criticism when they carry out so-called humanitarian operations. However, it is well known that some NGOs pick up migrants a few kilometres off the African coast and take them back to Lampedusa in Europe.

These humanitarian operations can destabilise Member States such as Italy, Spain, France and Greece just as much as if they were organised directly by third countries. It is therefore essential to establish whether certain NGOs are exploiting migrants on behalf of states, whether European or not, by encouraging or facilitating their movement towards the EU’s external borders or to a Member State. 1.

Does the Commission support requiring NGOs to publish the funding they receive from any legal or natural person, private or public, European or foreign, in order to combat such exploitation effectively?
Is the Commission prepared to launch infringement proceedings against European states which fund NGOs that destabilise other Member States by facilitating the arrival of migrants on their territory?
answer: EN on behalf of the Commission (19.6.2024) In line with the Financial Regulation1, the Commission publishes information on beneficiaries of EU funds, for the actions that it manages directly, in the Financial Transparency System2. In shared management mode, the Commission does not hold information at individual project level.

The managing authority in each Member State is in charge of the management of the funding, including the selection, contracting and payments to beneficiaries, according to shared management rules and the strategy defined in the Member State’s national programme.

More generally, when non-governmental organisations implement projects under Member States’ national programmes, they are neither selected by the Commission nor do they receive financial contribution directly from the Commission. Information on projects in shared management mode can be found through Member States’ national authorities3 in charge of the management of the funding.
1 Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 July 2018 on the

financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union, amending Regulations (EU) No 1296/2013, (EU) No 1301/2013, (EU) No 1303/2013, (EU) No 1304/2013, (EU) No 1309/2013, (EU) No 1316/2013, (EU) No 223/2014, (EU) No 283/2014, and Decision No 541/2014/EU and repealing Regulation (EU, Euratom) No 966/2012, OJ L 193, 30.7.2018, p. 1, Article 38. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/budget/financial-transparency-system/ 3 https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/funding_en
